definition: the two matched loads, eighteen years apart, that give the size of the drop

settled:
At twenty I carried six months of the heaviest social load there is, daily: knocking on doors and stopping people in the street, in a language not mine. Then I broke.

At my low point, less than ninety minutes of the same kind of load reached the same breaking line.

The ninety minutes is not a clean reading of that load alone. It is the whole cost of the breaking event it sat in, which carried lighter loads alongside the social one, and the social part was probably a tenth of it.

So taking the two figures at face value overstates the fall by about tenfold. The calibrated drop is a hundredfold.

title: The Experiment That Measured The Fall
